name: Mariner 2
first: NASA calls it the very first successful planetary science mission in history
description: Mariner 2 launched on 1962-08-27 on an Atlas-Agena B and passed Venus on 1962-12-14, at a closest approach of 34,773 km. Its magnetometer, particle detectors, solar plasma spectrometer, dust detector and two radiometers returned a first look at Venus: NASA reports temperatures from 216 °C on the dark side to 237 °C on the day side, a dense cloud layer 56 to 80 km up, a slow retrograde rotation, an atmosphere of mostly carbon dioxide and no discernible magnetic field. In space it showed that the solar wind streams continuously. Contact ended on 1963-01-03. NASA says that it keeps the honor of being the very first successful planetary science mission in history.
